cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. That is below the 40 to 60% typically seen in production systems of comparable complexity, and it means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete. This represents a single point of failure during both normal deployments and incident response, with no mitigation underway.

evidence_before_interpretation.detail: first sentence contains no concrete figure, expected one for this case's facts: 'Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure.'

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: The production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover process, and that engineer operates under a rolling month-to-month contract. A departure — whether planned, medical, or involuntary — would leave the company unable to access its own production data without credential reset, creating an uncontrolled outage window. There is no compensating control. The company should establish a credential-rotation schedule, implement a documented handover process triggered by contract renewal or notice, and move database access behind a secrets manager with audit logging and shared responsibility.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. There is no process for handling a data-subject deletion request, which exposes the company to liability under GDPR, CCPA, and similar regimes that grant individuals the right to erasure. Data subjects cannot exercise rights the company has no mechanism to fulfill.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no gate in continuous integration to block deployments below a defined threshold. The three production incidents over the past year all originated in untested edge cases that automated tests would have caught. Deployments are performed manually with no documented rollback procedure, which means a regression that reaches production cannot be quickly reversed. The combination of low coverage, the absence of any automation block, and manual deployment with no recovery path creates a direct line from code changes to customer impact.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. This means an attacker with database read access can obtain valid credentials for every user account without further effort, and those credentials are likely reused across other systems. There is no compensating control. Any database breach exposes the entire user base to account takeover across the company's applications and potentially external services.

Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. A production incident therefore requires that same engineer to be available, and remediation depends on their familiarity with the system state at that moment rather than on a tested process. The absence of a rollback procedure means a failed deployment may be harder to undo than to fix forward, extending the window of unavailability.

Code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase with no linting rule to enforce a convention. This creates friction during code review, where stylistic corrections compete with substantive ones, and makes the codebase harder to navigate for engineers unfamiliar with each section's local standards. Adopting a comment style guide and enforcing it via lint would eliminate this category of review friction at negligible cost.
